title: SharePoint: new SharePoint experience with Discover, Publish and Build in a redesigned app bar
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents the Copilot licence needed for AI features in Build and the Copilot Credits required for advanced site creation, which the briefing reports as unpublished. Microsoft also explains the signals used by Discover, contrary to the briefing's claim that content selection is undocumented. The roadmap facts and published automation commands check out.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The interface is inside licensed SharePoint, and users need an assigned licence that includes SharePoint.
claims.quote: To access SharePoint, users in your organization need to be assigned a license that includes SharePoint.

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no licence or add-on requirement specific to the new SharePoint experience.
claims.quote: To see these AI features in Build (for example, create sites with AI or AI actions like improve your site), your organization needs to assign a Copilot license to you.
claims.fix: Retain licensing.model as included for the interface redesign. Replace the broad absence in licensing.notes and the cost rationale with: 'Microsoft publishes no separate licence for the interface redesign; AI features in Build require an assigned Copilot licence.' Cite https://support.microsoft.com/office/cb17406a-59ea-488a-beb5-f8160af3ecb5.

claims.claim: The New SharePoint Experience page itself names no other licence.
claims.quote: Searched: 'new SharePoint experience license pricing meter Copilot Publish Build'; opened enable-new-sharepoint-experience in full and the SharePoint service description. The feature overview lists five interface changes and no licence requirement.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no meter for the interface redesign itself.
claims.quote: Searched: 'new SharePoint experience license pricing meter Copilot Publish Build'; opened the feature overview, service description, Discover, Build, Publish and Copilot in SharePoint. Billing is stated for Copilot capabilities, not the interface redesign.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; Open questions: AI-assisted creation
claims.claim: Whether AI-assisted creation reached from Build requires a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence is not yet published.
claims.quote: To see these AI features in Build (for example, create sites with AI or AI actions like improve your site), your organization needs to assign a Copilot license to you.
claims.fix: Replace the licence uncertainty with: 'AI features in Build, including creating sites with AI and improving a site, require an assigned Copilot licence.' Cite https://support.microsoft.com/office/cb17406a-59ea-488a-beb5-f8160af3ecb5. Remove Build's licence requirement from the corresponding open question; do not generalise this requirement to all Publish functions.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; Open questions: AI-assisted creation
claims.claim: Whether AI-assisted site creation reached from Build consumes Copilot Credits is not yet published.
claims.quote: Advanced work requires usage-based billing and consumes Copilot Credits. Requires Copilot Credits: Create entire sites and solutions.
claims.fix: Replace the site-creation billing uncertainty with: 'Creating entire sites and solutions with Copilot in SharePoint is advanced work that consumes Copilot Credits and requires usage-based billing enabled through a spending policy.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/copilot-in-sharepoint-get-started. Remove that already answered part of the open question; retain cost low for the interface redesign, not for optional advanced AI work.

claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint Discover experience how content selected personalized recommended'; read enable-new-sharepoint-experience in full. Its five changes concern Discover, the app bar, destinations, global navigation and theming; no new data source is named.

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no tenant UI or API switch to turn on, defer or turn off the launched interface redesign.
claims.quote: Searched: 'new SharePoint experience disable opt out tenant settings PowerShell Discover Publish Build'; opened the feature overview, app bar and Set-SPOTenant reference. No current GA switch found in documentation; a community Q&A discusses a former preview setting.

claims.claim: There is no documented UI or API control to hide individual app bar destinations such as Publish and Build.
claims.quote: Searched: 'new SharePoint experience disable opt out tenant settings PowerShell Discover Publish Build'; opened the app bar and Set-SPOTenant reference. The app bar documentation expressly says specific tabs cannot be disabled.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Specific app bar tabs cannot be disabled, irrespective of site creation policy.
claims.quote: Specific SharePoint app bar tabs can't be disabled.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The app bar cannot be disabled on specific sites.
claims.quote: The SharePoint app bar can't be disabled on specific sites.

claims.claim: The site creation control is at SharePoint admin center > Settings > Site creation > Control site creation from tools.
claims.quote: Go to Settings in the SharePoint admin center. Select Site creation. To allow users to create sites, select Allow under Control site creation from tools.
claims.fix: Extend controls[2].ui.path to 'Settings > Site creation > Control site creation from tools > Allow' as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/manage-site-creation. The existing route correctly reaches the setting's section.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -SelfServiceSiteCreationDisabled $true disables self-service site creation from the listed tools.
claims.quote:
### -SelfServiceSiteCreationDisabled
When set to True, users cannot create sites from SharePoint, OneDrive, the PnP PowerShell cmdlet, and the REST API.

claims.where: controls[2].governs; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The existing self-service site creation control applies to site creation from Build.
claims.quote: If the Site card is greyed out in the Start building section, self-service site creation might be disabled in SharePoint. If you're a tenant administrator, see Manage site creation in SharePoint
claims.fix: Add https://support.microsoft.com/office/cb17406a-59ea-488a-beb5-f8160af3ecb5 to sources: it explicitly links Build's disabled Site card to the existing self-service site creation setting.

claims.claim: Control site creation from tools covers SharePoint, OneDrive, PnP PowerShell and the REST API.
claims.quote: This setting controls whether users can create sites from SharePoint, OneDrive, the PnP PowerShell cmdlet, and the REST API.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Disabling site creation does not prevent Microsoft 365 group creation or group-dependent resources such as Teams.
claims.quote: Disabling site creation for users doesn't remove their ability to create Microsoft 365 groups or resources, such as Microsoft Teams, that rely on a group.

claims.claim: SharePoint Administrators and above can manage site creation settings.
claims.quote: As a SharePoint Administrator and above in Microsoft 365, you can let your users create and manage their own SharePoint sites.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no admin UI setting for SPFx placeholder positioning relative to elevated content.
claims.quote: Searched: 'DisableSpfxTopBottomPlaceholdersInElevatedContent admin center settings'; opened Set-SPOTenant and the New SharePoint Experience overview. Results document the PowerShell parameter, not an admin UI route.

claims.where: controls[3].api; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -DisableSpfxTopBottomPlaceholdersInElevatedContent $true controls SPFx top and bottom placeholder positioning.
claims.quote:
### -DisableSpfxTopBottomPlaceholdersInElevatedContent
This feature allows SharePoint Administrators to control where SPFx Top and Bottom placeholders are rendered in relation to elevated content.

claims.claim: True renders SPFx top and bottom placeholders outside elevated content.
claims.quote: Accepts a value of true to render the Top and Bottom placeholders outside the elevated content area

claims.claim: False renders SPFx top and bottom placeholders inside elevated content.
claims.quote: or false to render them inside the elevated content area

claims.claim: DisableSpfxTopBottomPlaceholdersInElevatedContent defaults to false.
claims.quote: By default, this feature is set to false.

claims.claim: A SharePoint Online administrator is required to run Set-SPOTenant.
claims.quote: You must be a SharePoint Online administrator to run the cmdlet.

claims.claim: A home site can be added through SharePoint admin center > Settings > Home sites > Add.
claims.quote: Select Settings, and then select Home sites. Select Add, and then select Use an existing communication site.
claims.fix: Extend controls[4].ui.path to 'Settings > Home sites > Add > Use an existing communication site'. The existing route stops early on the correct page; the cited page then asks for the communication site's URL and Save.

claims.claim: Set-SPOHomeSite -HomeSiteUrl <home site URL> designates the supplied site as a home site.
claims.quote: Use this cmdlet to set a SharePoint Site as a Home Site. -HomeSiteUrl: Sets the URL of the site collection to be the home site.

claims.claim: A SharePoint home site is a communication site.
claims.quote: A home site is a communication site that you create and set as the top landing page for all users in your intranet.

claims.claim: Managing home sites in the SharePoint admin center requires SharePoint admin or higher.
claims.quote: Sign in to the SharePoint admin center as a SharePoint admin or higher.

claims.claim: The New SharePoint Experience overview itself does not list which AI features are included.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint Publish Copilot license new experience'; read enable-new-sharepoint-experience in full. Its introduction says AI-first capabilities are built in but its five-item list names no specific AI capability; linked destination pages give more detail.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, group creation
claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to restrict Microsoft 365 group creation separately, but the controls table has no group creation row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'restrict Microsoft 365 group creation separately if that is the goal'. The six control rows cover the redesign, tabs, site creation, SPFx placeholders, home sites and global navigation, not group creation.
claims.fix: Remove 'restrict Microsoft 365 group creation separately if that is the goal' from the checklist. Keep the documented distinction between site creation and group creation in the control note and explanatory prose; do not add a row.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout, home site permissions
claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to grant home site read access, but the controls table has no site access row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Give users read access to the home site so they can see the global navigation links'. The global navigation row controls the navigation toggle, not the home site's access permissions.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullet 'Give users read access to the home site so they can see the global navigation links'. Retain read access as the documented prerequisite in Scope; do not add a row.
